claim_text: Perseus continued to roll out our Safely Home Every Day (SHED) and Fatality Risk Management programmes during the year, which have driven such positive outcomes at our sites.
context_text:
In FY25, our safety performance across the Group continued to improve with a significant step change year on year with strong outcomes:
TOTAL RECORDABLE INJURY FREQUENCY RATE (TRIFR) WAS 0.60;
43% improvement on FY24 (FY24 TRIFR: 1.06)
There were eight recordable injuries recorded across both employees and contractors
LOST TIME INJURY FREQUENCY RATE (LTIFR) WAS 0.08;
47% improvement on FY24 (FY24 LTIFR: 0.15)
Zero fatalities among our employees and contractors
label: Partially Supported
rationale_short: The report shows improved safety outcomes, but the causal statement that SHED and Fatality Risk Management programmes drove these results is not directly demonstrated.
llm_reason: The claim’s decisive assertion is that rolling out the SHED and Fatality Risk Management programmes “have driven such positive outcomes” at sites (i.e., the programmes caused improved safety results). The evidence substantiates the “positive outcomes” portion by reporting improved safety performance year-on-year: TRIFR decreased from 1.06 (FY24) to 0.60 (FY25), described as a 43% improvement; LTIFR decreased from 0.15 (FY24) to 0.08 (FY25), described as a 47% improvement; and there were zero fatalities in FY25 (with eight recordable injuries). However, the evidence does not substantively link these outcomes to the SHED and Fatality Risk Management programme rollout (no description of rollout extent/timing, implementation details, or evidence attributing causation), so the causal “have driven” element is not verified.
